name: Foundation 50
description: Audited 50-sense sample that proves search, study, audio, and backup.

senses.glossEn: A hand tool with a toothed blade, used for cutting wood or other hard material.
senses.glossTc: 有鋸齒的手工具，用來鋸開木材或其他硬物。
senses.usageNote: This is a tool. It is not the past of see.

examples.en: He used a saw to cut the shelf to size.
examples.tc: 他用鋸子把層板鋸成所需長度。

synonyms.difference: A handsaw is one common type of saw, not every cutting tool.

senses.glossEn: Past tense of see: noticed or looked at someone or something.
senses.glossTc: see 的過去式：看見或注意到某人或某物。
senses.usageNote: Same spelling as the tool. The headword is see.

examples.en: I saw the email this morning but have not replied yet.
examples.tc: 我今早看到那封電郵，但還未回覆。

senses.glossEn: To look at written words and understand their meaning.
senses.glossTc: 看文字並理解其意思。

examples.en: Please read the contract before you sign it.
examples.tc: 請先閱讀合約，再簽署。

synonyms.difference: Go through often means examine in detail, not only decode the words.

senses.glossEn: Past tense of read: finished looking at and understanding a text.
senses.glossTc: read 的過去式：已經看過並理解某段文字。
senses.usageNote: Spelling matches the present verb; the vowel sound changes.

examples.en: I read your proposal last night and marked two questions.
examples.tc: 我昨晚已讀過你的建議書，並標了兩個問題。

senses.glossEn: A business that keeps money, makes payments, and lends money.
senses.glossTc: 保管金錢、處理付款及借貸的機構。

examples.en: The shop pays takings into the bank every evening.
examples.tc: 店舖每晚都會把營業額存入銀行。

synonyms.difference: A lender may be a bank, but a bank also holds deposits and runs accounts.

senses.glossEn: The land along the side of a river or canal.
senses.glossTc: 河或運河兩旁的岸邊土地。
senses.usageNote: Do not treat this as the financial institution.

examples.en: We walked along the river bank after lunch.
examples.tc: 午飯後我們沿河岸散步。

synonyms.difference: Shore is more often used for a sea or lake than a river.

senses.glossEn: To shut something, or to bring a matter to an end.
senses.glossTc: 關上某物，或把一件事結束。

examples.en: Please close the till before you leave the shop.
examples.tc: 離開店舖前請關好收銀機。

synonyms.difference: Shut is usually physical. Close can also end a deal or a file.

senses.glossEn: Near in space, time, or relationship.
senses.glossTc: 在距離、時間或關係上接近。

examples.en: The warehouse is close to the MTR station.
examples.tc: 貨倉鄰近港鐵站。

synonyms.difference: Near is mainly about distance. Close can also describe a relationship.

senses.glossEn: To arrange in advance to have a place, time, or service.
senses.glossTc: 預先安排位置、時間或服務。

examples.en: Can you book a meeting room for Thursday morning?
examples.tc: 你能否預訂星期四上午的會議室？

synonyms.difference: Reserve is slightly more formal; both can mean hold a place.

senses.glossEn: To examine something so you know it is correct or complete.
senses.glossTc: 檢查某事物，確認它正確或齊全。

examples.en: Check the stock count before we open tomorrow.
examples.tc: 明天開店前先核對存貨數目。

synonyms.difference: Verify stresses proving that something is true, not only looking at it.

senses.glossEn: To give attention to a problem and start dealing with it.
senses.glossTc: 正視問題並着手處理。

examples.en: We need to address the delay before it affects the launch.
examples.tc: 我們要先處理延誤，以免影響推出時間。

synonyms.difference: Deal with is more general. Address often names the issue first.

senses.glossEn: Happening or being used now.
senses.glossTc: 現正發生或現正使用的。

examples.en: The current price list replaces last month's version.
examples.tc: 現行價目表已取代上個月的版本。

synonyms.difference: Present can also mean in the room. Current usually means latest.

senses.glossEn: The speaker or writer; used to talk about yourself.
senses.glossTc: 說話或書寫的人用來指自己。

examples.en: I will send the file after lunch.
examples.tc: 我午飯後會把檔案寄出。

senses.glossEn: The person or people being spoken or written to.
senses.glossTc: 指正在對話或收信的對方。

examples.en: Can you confirm the delivery time?
examples.tc: 你能否確認送貨時間？

senses.glossEn: The speaker and at least one other person.
senses.glossTc: 指自己連同至少另一人。

examples.en: We should test the till before Saturday.
examples.tc: 我們應在星期六前先測試收銀機。

senses.glossEn: People or things already known in the conversation, not you or me.
senses.glossTc: 指對話中已知、但不是你或我的人或事物。

examples.en: They asked for a refund this afternoon.
examples.tc: 他們今天下午要求退款。

senses.glossEn: To make a process simpler and faster by removing extra steps.
senses.glossTc: 精簡流程，去掉多餘步驟，使其更快捷。

examples.en: We should streamline the approval process before automating it.
examples.tc: 我們應先簡化審批流程，再將其自動化。

synonyms.difference: Simplify can mean make easier to understand. Streamline usually means remove delay from a process.

senses.glossEn: A series of steps used to get a result at work.
senses.glossTc: 為達成結果而設的一連串步驟。

examples.en: The refund process takes two working days.
examples.tc: 退款流程需時兩個工作天。

synonyms.difference: A procedure is often a written rule. A process is the work as it actually happens.

senses.glossEn: To officially agree that something may go ahead.
senses.glossTc: 正式同意某事可以進行。

examples.en: The manager will approve the discount if it stays under ten percent.
examples.tc: 只要折扣不超過一成，經理便會批准。

synonyms.difference: Authorise stresses giving permission. Approve can also mean judge something as acceptable.

senses.glossEn: The latest time by which work must be finished.
senses.glossTc: 工作必須完成的最後期限。

examples.en: The report deadline is Friday at 5 p.m.
examples.tc: 報告截止日期是星期五下午五時。

synonyms.difference: Due date is common for bills and homework. Deadline is common for work tasks.

senses.glossEn: A person or group affected by a project and able to influence it.
senses.glossTc: 受項目影響、亦能影響項目的人或團體。

examples.en: Shop staff are stakeholders in the new till system.
examples.tc: 店舖同事也是新收銀系統的持份者。

synonyms.difference: Interested party is legal wording. Stakeholder is everyday project language.

senses.glossEn: What a project will and will not include.
senses.glossTc: 項目包括和不包括的範圍。

examples.en: Training videos are outside the scope of this week's work.
examples.tc: 培訓影片不在本週工作範圍內。

synonyms.difference: Range is general size. Scope names agreed project boundaries.

senses.glossEn: A possible problem that could harm a plan if it happens.
senses.glossTc: 一旦發生便可能損害計劃的潛在問題。

examples.en: Late stock delivery is the main risk this month.
examples.tc: 貨物遲送是本月的主要風險。

synonyms.difference: A threat is often more hostile. A risk can be an ordinary delay or cost.

senses.glossEn: To give the latest information, or to change something so it is current.
senses.glossTc: 提供最新資料，或把事物改成最新狀態。

examples.en: Please update the team after you speak to the supplier.
examples.tc: 與供應商談完後，請向團隊匯報最新情況。

synonyms.difference: Inform can be any news. Update means the news is newer than before.

senses.glossEn: A planned time when people talk about work together.
senses.glossTc: 預先安排、一起討論工作的時間。

examples.en: The supplier meeting starts at ten.
examples.tc: 供應商會議十時開始。

synonyms.difference: A discussion can be informal. A meeting is usually scheduled.

senses.glossEn: A finished piece of work that you have promised to hand over.
senses.glossTc: 已承諾要交出的完成工作成果。

examples.en: The first deliverable is a one-page process map.
examples.tc: 第一項交付成果是一頁流程圖。

synonyms.difference: Output is any result. A deliverable is an agreed hand-over.

senses.glossEn: A person who buys goods or services from a shop or business.
senses.glossTc: 向店舖或公司購買貨品或服務的人。

examples.en: A regular customer asked about the new opening hours.
examples.tc: 一位熟客詢問新的營業時間。

synonyms.difference: Client is more common for professional services. Customer is more common in shops.

senses.glossEn: A bill that lists what was sold and how much must be paid.
senses.glossTc: 列出已售項目及應付款額的帳單。

examples.en: Please send the invoice to the accounts email.
examples.tc: 請把發票寄到會計電郵。

synonyms.difference: Bill is everyday. Invoice is the formal document used between businesses.

senses.glossEn: Money a business receives from sales before costs are taken off.
senses.glossTc: 扣除成本前，生意從銷售收到的金錢。

examples.en: Weekend revenue rose after we extended opening hours.
examples.tc: 延長營業時間後，週末收入上升。

synonyms.difference: Income can include wages or rent. Revenue usually means sales money.

senses.glossEn: A written plan offered for other people to accept or reject.
senses.glossTc: 供對方接受或拒絕的書面計劃。

examples.en: Her proposal explains how the shop can cut waiting time.
examples.tc: 她的建議書說明店舖如何縮短等候時間。

synonyms.difference: A plan can stay internal. A proposal is offered to someone else.

senses.glossEn: Comments on how well something worked, used to improve it.
senses.glossTc: 關於效果好壞的意見，用來改進。

examples.en: Customer feedback said the queue felt too long.
examples.tc: 顧客意見指排隊時間令人覺得太長。

synonyms.difference: Comments can be any remarks. Feedback is given so work can improve.

senses.glossEn: Money paid back to a customer.
senses.glossTc: 退回給顧客的金錢。

examples.en: We issued a refund after the item arrived damaged.
examples.tc: 貨品送達時已損壞，我們已辦理退款。

synonyms.difference: Reimbursement often pays back a cost someone already spent. A refund returns a purchase price.

senses.glossEn: A line of people waiting for their turn.
senses.glossTc: 輪候的一排人。

examples.en: The lunch queue reached the door by twelve.
examples.tc: 中午十二時，午膳排隊已排到門口。

synonyms.difference: Line is more common in American English. Queue is the usual British and Hong Kong word.

senses.glossEn: How something feels to a person while they use a shop or service.
senses.glossTc: 顧客使用店舖或服務時的感受。

examples.en: A slow queue can spoil an otherwise good shopping experience.
examples.tc: 排隊太慢，即使其他環節不錯，購物體驗也會變差。

synonyms.difference: An impression is a first judgment. Experience covers the whole visit.

senses.glossEn: A statement that something is wrong or not good enough.
senses.glossTc: 指某事有問題或未達標準的陳述。

examples.en: We logged the complaint and offered a replacement the same day.
examples.tc: 我們已記錄投訴，並在當日提供更換。

synonyms.difference: An objection is often raised in a meeting. A complaint is usually about service or a product.

senses.glossEn: To start selling or offering something new in public.
senses.glossTc: 公開推出新產品或新服務。

examples.en: We will launch the new loyalty card in October.
examples.tc: 我們將於十月推出新的會員卡。

synonyms.difference: Release is common for software. Launch often includes the public start.

senses.glossEn: To change the main direction of a business when the first plan is not working.
senses.glossTc: 原計劃行不通時，改變生意的主要方向。

examples.en: They pivoted from a food stall to weekend catering.
examples.tc: 他們由小吃攤轉向週末到會。

synonyms.difference: Change course is ordinary English. Pivot is business slang for a planned turn.

senses.glossEn: The money moving in and out of a business over a period.
senses.glossTc: 一段時間內流入和流出生意的現金。
senses.usageNote: Phrase frequency is not manufactured from cash + flow.

examples.en: Slow cash flow made it hard to pay the supplier early.
examples.tc: 現金流偏慢，難以提早支付供應商。

synonyms.difference: Liquidity is a finance term for how easily assets become cash. Cash flow is the actual movement of money.

senses.glossEn: To make a machine or program do work that people used to do by hand.
senses.glossTc: 改由機器或程式完成以往人手做的工作。

examples.en: Do not automate a messy process; clean it first.
examples.tc: 不要先把混亂流程自動化；應先理順。

synonyms.difference: Computerise means put work on a computer. Automate means the computer then does the steps.

senses.glossEn: To put a system or update into real use.
senses.glossTc: 把系統或更新正式投入使用。

examples.en: We will deploy the till update after closing time.
examples.tc: 我們會在關門後部署收銀系統更新。

synonyms.difference: Roll out often means introduce to users in stages. Deploy is the technical put-live step.

senses.glossEn: A copy of files kept so work can be restored if the original is lost.
senses.glossTc: 另存的檔案副本，以便原本遺失時還原。

examples.en: Keep a backup of your study file outside this phone.
examples.tc: 請在這部手機以外另存學習檔備份。

synonyms.difference: Any copy is a copy. A backup exists specifically for recovery.

senses.glossEn: Not connected to the internet, but still able to use saved material.
senses.glossTc: 未連接互聯網，但仍可使用已儲存的資料。
senses.usageNote: No useful interchangeable synonym. Opposite of online.

examples.en: The installed pack works offline after you prepare it.
examples.tc: 完成準備後，已安裝的內容可離線使用。

senses.glossEn: To arrange for something to happen at a particular time.
senses.glossTc: 安排某事在指定時間發生。

examples.en: Let's schedule the staff briefing for Monday morning.
examples.tc: 我們把員工簡介安排在星期一上午。

synonyms.difference: Arrange is broader. Schedule always sets a time.

senses.glossEn: To say that something is true or definitely arranged.
senses.glossTc: 表明某事屬實，或已確定安排。

examples.en: Please confirm that the Saturday shift is covered.
examples.tc: 請確認星期六的更期已有人頂。

synonyms.difference: Verify checks evidence. Confirm can also mean give a definite yes.

senses.glossEn: To discuss terms until both sides can accept an agreement.
senses.glossTc: 雙方商討條件，直至可以接受協議。

examples.en: We negotiated a longer payment period with the supplier.
examples.tc: 我們與供應商談妥較長的付款期。

synonyms.difference: Bargain often means argue over price. Negotiate can cover time, scope, or terms.

senses.glossEn: To contact someone again about a matter that is not finished.
senses.glossTc: 就尚未完成的事情再次聯絡對方。
senses.usageNote: Phrase frequency is not manufactured from follow + up.

examples.en: I will follow up with the supplier if we have no reply by noon.
examples.tc: 若中午前仍未回覆，我會再跟供應商跟進。

synonyms.difference: Chase is informal and can sound impatient. Follow up is the usual workplace wording.

senses.glossEn: A polite word used when asking for something.
senses.glossTc: 提出要求時表示禮貌的用語。

examples.en: Please wait here while I check the stockroom.
examples.tc: 請在這裏稍候，我去貨倉查看。

senses.glossEn: To tell someone you are grateful.
senses.glossTc: 向對方表示感謝。

examples.en: Thank the customer before you hand over the bag.
examples.tc: 把袋子交給顧客前，先向對方道謝。

senses.glossEn: To make it easier for someone to do something.
senses.glossTc: 協助別人，使事情較容易完成。

examples.en: I can help you find a smaller size.
examples.tc: 我可以幫你找細一碼。

synonyms.difference: Assist is more formal. Help is the ordinary word.

senses.glossEn: Used to apologise or to show you regret a problem.
senses.glossTc: 用來道歉，或表示對問題感到抱歉。

examples.en: Sorry for the wait; the next till is opening now.
examples.tc: 抱歉讓你等候；下一個收銀櫃位現正開放。
